title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says the company will pick humanity over share price, investors
source_used: Vanity Fair interview with Sam Altman, Part 1 (https://www.vanityfair.com/story/sam-altman-exclusive-interview-part-1), read in full; Yahoo Finance's write-up of it (the pool item) read for its added context
key_facts: Vanity Fair published a two-part interview with OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman on 5 Oct 2026; the talks were held in San Francisco on 11 Sep and 2 Oct.

Asked whether going public would change the company, which began as a nonprofit and later converted to a for-profit structure, Altman said OpenAI will still have a nonprofit that governs it even after it goes public, 'which we are not in a rush to do'.

Altman: 'we will remind investors and anyone that thinks about buying our shares that we are going to put the mission first'; he believes this is compatible with shareholders doing 'super well', but 'if they're ever in tension, the mission is going to come first'.
Asked what happens if the stock price falls because profit benchmarks are missed, Altman answered 'Then it falls. Maybe it falls a lot. I don't know.'

Altman: if AI progress turned out to be incompatible with making an incredibly valuable company, 'we are clearly going to pick doing the right thing for humanity'; he says he does not think that is the case.
Altman said OpenAI has made decisions that mean 'going slower on revenue than we otherwise could' and that 'we've slowed down'.
Yahoo Finance adds that OpenAI is widely expected to go public in early 2027 and that rival Anthropic is rumoured to be preparing a listing ahead of Thanksgiving.

why_it_matters_hint: The head of OpenAI states, before any listing, that the mission comes before shareholders if the two conflict; it is a promise, not yet tested.
event_date: Interview published 5 Oct 2026; held 11 Sep and 2 Oct 2026 (the transcript does not say which session this answer came from)
notes: Pool item is Yahoo Finance's own write-up (Daniel Howley) of the Vanity Fair interview. The Vanity Fair interview itself was read, matches the quotes, and is credited and linked as the first reporter. Yahoo's added context is attributed to Yahoo. Fortune (5 Oct) separately reports that Altman said OpenAI will not go public this year.
